node.label: Joanna Bourke
node.date_label: Dismembering the Male (1996) · An Intimate History of Killing (1999) · Fear: A Cultural History (2005)
node.description: A historian of modern Britain, war, the body and emotion. Dismembering the Male (1996) studies men’s bodies and masculinity in the First World War. An Intimate History of Killing (1999), drawing on letters, diaries and memoirs of British, American and Australian combatants in the two world wars and Vietnam, argues that the structure of war encouraged pleasure in killing and that ordinary men could become enthusiastic killers without being brutalized. Her later work on fear and pain asks what emotions do: expressions of fear follow learned conventions yet can change the feeling they name, a point she develops through William Reddy’s concept of the emotive.
